blocks.text: It states that the sum of all the currents meeting at a point in the circuit is zero.
It is a convention that a current flowing towards a point is taken as positive and that flowing away from a point is taken as negative.

blocks.title: For Your Information
blocks.text: A node is a point in an electric circuit which joins the two or more branches.
Consider a situation where four wires meet at a point A (Fig. 9.27). The currents flowing into the point A are I₁ and I₂ and currents flowing away from the point are I₃ and I₄.

blocks.alt: Four wires, each containing a resistor, meet at a point A. Arrows show currents I1 (from the left) and I2 (from the lower left) flowing towards A, and currents I3 (to the lower right) and I4 (to the upper right) flowing away from A.
blocks.caption: Figure 9.27: According to Kirchhoff's 1st rule I1 + I2 = I3 + I4 (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 9.27).

blocks.title: Do You Know?
blocks.text: The node, which potential is taken as zero is called datum node.

blocks.title: Kirchhoff's first rule
blocks.text: The sum of all the currents flowing towards a point is equal to the sum of all the currents flowing away from the point.

Kirchhoff's first rule which is also known as Kirchhoff's point rule is a manifestation of law of conservation of charge. If there is no sink or source of charge at a point, the total charge flowing towards the point must be equal to the total charge flowing away from it.
